correctness.rationale: Independent computation built the closed balls from pairwise Hamming distances. It eliminated only redundant supersets among the hitting requirements and split an unmet requirement by the first chosen element (forbidding earlier choices in each branch), so no completion is lost or counted twice. For reversal the same construction uses one decision per orbit weighted by 1 or 2. Stopping at the first feasible budget counts the entire minimum layer: stopping at a proper subset cannot hide a minimum solution. Direct signature tests were applied to all returned codes. The n=1 neighborhoods coincide. The independently reproduced (ordinary minimum, count; invariant minimum, count) for n=2–7 are (2,1;2,1), (3,6;3,2), (4,14;4,2), (5,2;6,8), (8,18;8,2), (12,13;12,5). For n=7 there are 595 distinct nonempty requirements and 21 reversal blocks; the ordinary budgets 11 and 12 gave 0 and 13, and the entire 13-set layer matches the TSV. Fixed counts among unrestricted optima are 1,2,2,0,2,5; the involution gives 1,4,8,1,10,9 classes. The packaged secondary checker alone does not certify completeness of the unrestricted n=7 layer; the independent search does.

evidence: The distinct Lucas-cube record gives dihedral minima 8 at n=6 and 14 at n=7, compared with its unrestricted minima 7 and 11; the Fibonacci result has no penalty at either dimension. The hypercube record imposes coordinate-permutation invariance on unrestricted binary words. Ashrafi et al. give perfect-code existence iff n≤3.

value.rationale: This is a complete census across the stated consecutive initial dimensions of a standard graph family under its natural coordinate involution. It gives a sharp, nonmonotone symmetry obstruction: the first penalty occurs at five and is absent again at six and seven. The exact n=7 list and orbit counts distinguish abundance of minimum placements from abundance of symmetric ones and provide a reference for structural or algorithmic work. There is no claimed trend beyond seven.
residual_risks: Finite cutoff; no extrapolation to higher dimensions or sensing radii.
